name: 类型-标记比 (TTR)
description: Computes the ratio of unique words to total words using MATTR variant to detect AI-generated text's vocabulary patterns.
useCase: Detecting AI text through abnormal lexical diversity ratios across text segments
mechanism: Calculates the Moving-Average Type-Token Ratio (MATTR) using a sliding window approach to mitigate text length effects. For each window of N words, the ratio of unique types to total tokens is computed, then averaged. AI-generated text often exhibits more uniform TTR values across windows compared to human writing, which naturally varies in vocabulary richness between different sections due to topic shifts and stylistic changes.
source: Covington, M. A. & McFall, J. D. (2010) - Cutting the Gordian Knot: The Moving-Average Type-Token Ratio (MATTR), Journal of Quantitative Linguistics
algorithm: Moving-Average Type-Token Ratio (MATTR) + Variance Analysis + Segment Comparison
parameters: Window size: 50-100 tokens, Metrics: mean MATTR, MATTR variance, MATTR range, Normalization: length-independent
strengths:
• Length-independent measurement via MATTR
• Well-established psycholinguistic metric
• Fast computation with minimal resources
• Captures vocabulary usage patterns
limitations:
• Lower discriminative power as standalone feature
• Sensitive to text genre and topic
• Advanced LLMs increasingly match human TTR ranges
• Window size selection affects results

references.title: Covington, M. A. & McFall, J. D. (2010). Cutting the Gordian Knot: The Moving-Average Type-Token Ratio (MATTR). Journal of Quantitative Linguistics.
Tulchinskii, E. et al. (2024). Intrinsic Dimension Estimation for Robust Detection of AI-Generated Texts. NeurIPS.
